page: Amazon Web Services g5g.2xlarge is an ARM64-based server instance powered by an 8-core AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor running at 2.5 GHz. The instance features dedicated CPU allocation with one thread per core, 16.0 GB of system memory providing 2.0 GB per core, and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. It is equipped with a single NVIDIA Turing T4G GPU featuring 16 GB of VRAM. Local storage is not included on this instance.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across several compute and memory metrics, alongside notable weaknesses in specific workloads. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests yielded average scores of 1519.58 and 12132.81, respectively. Memory bandwidth tests show an average read-only small block speed of 472.81 GB/sec, though large block write speeds drop to 53.67 GB/sec. The instance demonstrates weak single-threaded performance, as seen in the Geekbench single-core score of 950.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 5224.12. Cryptographic operations represent a significant bottleneck, with the Passmark CPU encryption test scoring in the poor range at 1082.49.

The inclusion of the NVIDIA T4G GPU makes this instance suitable for graphics-intensive workloads, ray tracing, and image processing, which is supported by average Geekbench ray tracing (7109.0) and image processing (4112.0) scores. However, large language model inference performance is limited, with text generation speeds for a small 135M model reaching only 36.51 tokens/sec and a medium 7B model dropping to 6.16 tokens/sec. This hardware profile is suited for ARM-native graphics rendering, Android game streaming, and moderate GPU-accelerated workloads rather than heavy LLM deployment.
